$schema_note: Hand-curated record of the counts the unique picks are checked against, NOT mechanically extracted (see hs-game-sdk/curated/satanic_zone.json for why curated/ exists). Data only: no binding is generated from this file, and hs_game_sdk/unique_pick_model.py never reads it; tests/test_unique_pick_model.py reads both and checks that the model reproduces each entry. The mechanism, in our own words, is docs/models/unique-pick-spec.md, whose notation (T, L_k, D_k, c, e, n, m) the `model` fields use. Every entry has `id`, `kind` (`baseline` = vanilla, nothing pushed; `target` = a ForgePact lever applied; `our_code` = a contract of ForgePact's own code, not the game), `status` (`measured` or `our_code`), `date` (the measurement date; for `our_code` entries, the date the code was read), `source` (a list of {path, section} or {repo, commit}; paths are relative to the hub root, `section` is text that appears in that file), `scripts` (every `gml_Script_*` the entry involves, all bound in hs_game_sdk.scripts.GameScript), `what` (the observation), `values`, `model` (what the model must show) and, once the model's tests exist, exactly one of `reproduced_by` (the dotted id of the test that reproduces it) or `not_reproduced` (why it cannot be). Every #74 count below was made with the Angelic roll's chance raised by a research lever, never at the natural chance; `standinPicks=` is keyed on a stand-in's sub and b (the pair, not the triple), so its vanilla share is m / T. The flight charms' own live counts (UP9 to UP13, #158's Mod live 1 and Mod live 2) cite ForgePact/docs/flight-charms-research.md's Mod live 1 results and Mod live 2 results, where they are recorded; like #74's, they were made with the Angelic roll's chance raised by a research lever, the ordinary unique roll is called by name, and UP11's `flightprobe pool` pins T at 48. UP14 (ForgePact#166, the Mark 1 pieces on the Heroic roll) is the flight charms' Live 1 `heroic_route`, copied from hs-game-sdk/curated/flight_charms_measurements.json with its source: ten by-name DropItemHeroic calls with the player as self and nothing pushed; T_H, the entries the Heroic roll keeps, is not measured and stays a parameter. UP15 to UP20 (ForgePact#166, the kill's own draw inside DropItem) are Mark 1's Mod live procedure 7, three sessions on 2026-10-20 and 2026-10-21 (Live 1, 1b and 1c, slot 14, Hell), recorded in ForgePact/docs/mark1-set-research.md's Mod live 7 results and Phase 4 decision and folded into docs/RUNTIME_DATA_MODELS.md § 13.12; they use W_k (the acceptance-weighted entries of list k the draw keeps), n_k (a stand-in's own count on list k) and a (an entry's acceptance), the spec's notation for the draw. Live 1c ran at magic find x10, the other two at x1. The live captures are gitignored and never cited here.

source.section: ### 23.8 The ordinary unique roll makes one draw

measurements.what: #74 Live 2's list dump: Controller_obj.lootListUnique is an array of 6 ds_lists of 50, 61, 79, 152, 221 and 380 entries, every entry a triple; the sizes were the same after a zone change and at the end of the session. Only [5] holds Liquor Holster's {8, 0, 51}, once.
measurements.model: The ordinary roll's chance of dropping one entry pushed once onto sub-list k is 1 / (L_k + 1), between 1/51 and 1/222 over these lengths; with c copies it is c / (L_k + c). That holds if the roll's random index cannot equal the list's length (not established; if it can, the share is 1 in L_k + 2; the model keeps it open as `index_can_reach_length`, docs/models/unique-pick-spec.md § Not established).

source.section: How #74 uses the list: a stand-in entry for the length of the roll.
Elf's stand-in, Aimbot.exe, is on none of them

measurements.what: The push: for the length of one roll ForgePact adds c copies of each switched-on item's stand-in entry to the list that roll reads, and takes them off its tail afterwards. Headhunter, Tyrant's Crown, Gabriel Wings and Witch's Broomstick push onto lootListUnique[5] (the Angelic roll); Pocket Elf pushes onto each of lootListUnique[0..4] (the ordinary unique roll) and adds nothing inside the Angelic roll. c is a constexpr 1 in the player build for both #74 (g_SigCopies) and the flight charms (g_FlightDropCopies); only the research build's copies levers change it, 1 to 400. stand_ins lists one triple per item: the Wings' Water Melon and the Broomstick's Soul Collector are fixed in the code (kWingsStandIn, kBroomStandIn) and Headhunter's Liquor Holster is named in it and looked up in the validated Angelic pool; Tyrant's Crown's Mask of the Celestial and Pocket Elf's Aimbot.exe are chosen at runtime (the crown's as a helmet of the validated pool, the Elf's as the first of five candidates in kElfCandidates with an even count across lootListUnique[0..4]), so those two triples are the ones the live sessions recorded (#74's `stand-ins` lines; Mod live 2's `pool`).
measurements.model: As an input transform: an Angelic roll with these items on sees T + e droppable entries, e the sum of c over the items switched on; an ordinary roll with Pocket Elf on sees L_k + c entries on sub-list k. Switched off, nothing is added and the baseline shares are unchanged.

source.section: // The share of a stand-in hit that becomes the charm: c / (n + c).
a candidate is the mod item's with

measurements.what: The coin: a typed hit whose whole triple is a pushed stand-in's goes to the item with probability c / (n + c), n being how many vanilla entries of that list carry the same triple, and otherwise stays the game's own. Pocket Elf's stand-in is chosen so that n is the same on all five sub-lists.
measurements.model: As an input transform: the stand-in triple is kept with (n + c) / (T + e) and the coin gives the item c / (n + c) of that, so each item takes c / (T + e) of the Angelic roll's drops and the stand-in keeps n / (T + e); on the ordinary roll Pocket Elf takes c / (L_k + c). At c = 1 every item takes exactly one entry's share.

source.section: At the research lever's 200 copies, 20 unique-roll calls placed 19 items, 11 of them Pocket Elf
With 200 copies added, 20 calls placed 19 items, 11 of them the added

measurements.what: #158 Mod live 1 (S19, research dll c15f85e1..., Town_01_rm), Pocket Elf's switch on with Aimbot.exe as its stand-in and the research lever pushing 200 copies onto each of lootListUnique[0..4] per call (injected=20000 over 20 calls): 20 by-name calls of the ordinary unique roll placed 19 items, 11 of them Pocket Elf, ours equal to built (elf=11/11), refused=0, anomalies=0. Every hit line read the coin as 200 in 200, so the stand-in's n on the ordinary lists is 0.
measurements.model: With Pocket Elf pushed at c = 200 and n = 0, one call drops it with c / (L_k + c), between 200/421 and 200/250 over the five lengths, whichever list the roll chooses: 11 of 20 lies within the 3-sigma band over that range; the player build's one copy (1/222 to 1/51) and no push (0) are rejected.

source.section: and 21 Wings and 22 Broomsticks of 44, ours equal to built each time

measurements.what: #158 Mod live 1 (S20, research dll c15f85e1..., Act_01_01), Gabriel Wings' and Witch's Broomstick's switches on and 200 copies of each stand-in (Water Melon {10, 0, 47} and Soul Collector {10, 0, 91}) pushed onto lootListUnique[5] per roll, the Angelic roll's chance raised by a research lever: 44 rolls gave 44 hits, 21 of them Gabriel Wings and 22 Witch's Broomstick, ours equal to built, refused=0, anomalies=0 (after 26 hits, 13 of each). The hit lines read the coin as 200 in 201 (n = 1).

source.section: The Angelic roll's list held 380 entries, 48 of them

measurements.what: #158 Mod live 2 (`flightprobe pool`, research dll dd87086c..., read in Town_01_rm and again in Act_01_01 before the kills, both readings the same, nothing pushed): lootListUnique[5] held 380 entries, 48 of them droppable by the Angelic roll's tests (counted with repeats), with Water Melon and Soul Collector once each; the ordinary lists [0..4] held 50, 61, 79, 152 and 221 entries, and Pocket Elf's stand-in Aimbot.exe none of them.
measurements.model: T is 48: inside the 40..60 the #74 replays accepted, and every #74 count still fits the band at T = 48; n is 1 for both Angelic stand-ins and 0 for Pocket Elf's on every ordinary list, so the coin hands the flight charms 1 / 2 and 1 of a stand-in hit at c = 1, and each charm takes 1 / (48 + e) of the Angelic roll's drops.

source.section: At one copy, 100 unique-roll calls placed 97 items, one of them Pocket Elf
With one entry added to each sub-list per call, 100 calls placed 97

measurements.what: #158 Mod live 2 (`rate-elf`, research dll dd87086c..., Town_01_rm), Pocket Elf's switch on with Aimbot.exe as its stand-in and the player build's one copy pushed onto each of lootListUnique[0..4] per call (injected=500 over 100 calls): 100 by-name calls of the ordinary unique roll placed 97 items, one of them Pocket Elf, ours equal to built (elf=1/1), refused=0, anomalies=0. Before the switch went on, ten calls placed ten uniques and no Pocket Elf (unique-control).
measurements.model: With Pocket Elf pushed at c = 1 and n = 0, one call drops it with 1 / (L_k + 1), between 1/222 and 1/51: 1 of 100 lies within the 3-sigma band over that range (one entry's share); Mod live 1's 200 copies (200/421 to 200/250) and no push are rejected. At one copy the band is wide: one Pocket Elf in 100 calls cannot tell one entry's share from a share a few times larger or smaller, so this entry rules out only the 200-copy flood and no push at all; it does not pin the rate, and it does not settle whether the index can equal the length (1 / (L_k + 2)).

source.section: placed ten items: seven Heroic (9) and three Satanic (6), none Angelic or Unholy
seven Heroic (9) and three Satanic (6), none Angelic or Unholy

source.section: Live 1b read `on-k=` +8 and `off-k=` +0, and Live 1c `on-k=` +103 and `off-k=` +0
built at the k its triple sits on (k = 1: 22, k = 2: 5, k = 3: 14, k = 4:

measurements.what: Mod live 7, nothing pushed for these counts: an ordinary kill's unique is built by DropItem's own draw. In Live 1's owner window (about 10 minutes) all 4 natural uniques were built in the draw's scope, while DropUniqueItems, ReturnRandomSatanic and the builds outside DropItem each rose by 0 (unique-route: satanic-draw). Every natural draw build's triple sat on list k, k what LoadSatanicDropTier answered in the same call, and its tier equalled k (tier-k: matches): on-k 4 and off-k 0 in Live 1, on-k 8 and off-k 0 in Live 1b, on-k 103 and off-k 0 in Live 1c, whose natural draw builds came at k = 1 to 5 as 22, 5, 14, 59 and 3. A debugger logpoint on the draw's own CreateDefaultParams call hit once per draw build (4 of 4 in Live 1, 105 of 105 in Live 1c).
measurements.model: The draw reads list k with k in DRAW_LIST_INDICES (0 to 5), and list k holds the tier-k uniques: every natural draw build is counted on k (off_k = 0), its k is one of the six lists, and the k histogram adds up to the natural draw builds. Negative control: the DropUniqueItems roll's lists (0 to 4) cannot hold Live 1c's three builds at k = 5.

source.section: `reads=` 28, 9, 19 and 85 for the window's four draw builds
Their `reads=` run from 2 to 249, with a median of 3

measurements.what: Mod live 7, the GetUniqueRepoStruct reads in the draw's scope since the last build, for each natural draw build: 28, 9, 19 and 85 in Live 1's window and 4, 2, 5, 3, 2, 2, 4 and 3 in Live 1b, 12 builds with a median of 4; Live 1c's 103 ran from 2 to 249 with a median of 3. The Phase 4 rule reads a median of 10 or fewer, with the lever half below, as draw-mode: first-kept.
measurements.model: draw-mode is first-kept, the mode draw_share has a formula for: the 12 builds' median is 4, within the rule's 10. The reads include lookups other than the draw's own, so they bound how many entries the draw throws back, and do not measure W_k.

source.section: The below half's picks per typed draw build were 1 / 3 = 0.33
The mean list-k length over the `draw` builds was 274.0 in the below half

measurements.what: Mod live 7, Live 1b's below half (research build b46e5ab3..., magic find x1, the owner's play): the research lever pushed c = 25 copies of each of s = 4 below-SS stand-ins (helmet, body, boots and gloves, tiers 4, 4, 1 and 2) onto each of lootListUnique[0..5] for every DropItem call (push-held +971, equal to the calls, push-skipped +0), and the draw read pushed entries 1943 times. Of the half's 3 typed draw builds, 1 was a stand-in (picks +1, pick-builds +1): the gloves stand-in, built at k = 5 where no natural copy sits. The mean list-k length over those builds was 274.0, and after the lever was switched off the lists read 50, 61, 79, 152, 221 and 380 again.
measurements.model: Under first-kept, with each pushed entry kept as read (a = 1), the stand-ins take s*c / (W_k + s*c) of the draw's builds, at least s*c / (L_k + s*c) = 100 / 374 at the mean length since W_k is at most L_k: 1 of 3 lies within the 3-sigma band, and so does the Phase 4 rule's half of it (0.13). No push (a share of 0) is rejected. Three builds are a thin reading, as Phase 4 says.

source.section: Live 1c built 2 SS stand-ins among 105 draw builds at magic find x10,

measurements.what: Mod live 7, the SS halves: c = 25 copies of each of s = 4 SS stand-ins (rarity 6, tier 5: helmet 0:15, body 0:1, boots 0:9, gloves 0:16, each on lootListUnique[5] only; the helmet's and the boots' built lines read their counts on lists 0 to 5 as 0,0,0,0,0,1) pushed onto each of [0..5] per DropItem call. Live 1c (magic find x10, about 28 minutes, 8146 calls) built 105 uniques through the draw, 2 of them stand-ins (ss-build: seen): the helmet at k = 2 and the boots at k = 4, where no natural copy sits; the debugger's logpoint on the draw's build call hit 105 times. No natural rarity-6, tier-5 unique was built through the draw in that window. Live 1b's SS half (x1) built 6 through the draw, none a stand-in. The probe's picks= (47 and 13) is an instrument count, not the draw's picks, and is not used here.
measurements.model: With a = 1 the SS stand-ins would take at least 100 / (L_k + 100) of the draw's builds on any list, 100 / 480 on the longest: 2 of 105 lies far below that band, so a pushed SS entry the draw reads is kept with an acceptance well below 1. Why is not established, so a is an input; at W_k = L_k an acceptance of 1/100 fits the count. Live 1b's 0 of 6 cannot reject a = 1 (too few builds). The SS rate a piece gets is therefore taken from Live 2, not from the pick share.

source.section: inline double DrawCoinShare(const DrawPushEntry& e, int k)
inline double ElfDrawShare(const DrawStandIn& s, int k, int copies)

measurements.what: The draw push (kill-core, elf-core and adapter): for the length of each outermost DropItem call, with a feature's switch on, each resolved draw stand-in (one per Mark 1 piece, one for Pocket Elf) goes onto each of lootListUnique[0..5], c copies, c a constexpr 1 in the player build (kPlayerCopies through g_Mark1DropCopies, and g_FlightDropCopies); only the research build's copies levers change it, up to 400. A stand-in is a triple of the item's class the draw keeps as read (rarity 6, fields 40 and 41 clear): Mark 1 prefers an SS (tier 5) one and falls back below SS only for a class with none; Pocket Elf takes tier 5 only. A typed hit on a stand-in's whole triple is the item's with probability c / (n_k + c), k the tier LoadSatanicDropTier answered in the innermost DropItem call in progress and n_k the stand-in's own count on list k; with no tier recorded the hit is refused (tier-unread).
measurements.model: As an input transform: a call with the switches on adds p = c per resolved item to every list the draw can read; the stand-in triple is kept with (n_k + c) * a / (W_k + p) and the coin hands the item c / (n_k + c) of that, so each item takes c * a / (W_k + p) whichever k the call drew from. Switched off nothing is added, and every entry keeps its baseline r * a / W_k.
